index.title: Operations console
index.detailsSummary: Gifts, notifications and staff actions (last 7 days)

users.noEmail: No verified email; account recovery requires separate identity verification.

flags.hint: When on, all non-safe methods return 503 and the whole site is write-locked. Current state: {state}.
flags.auditNote: All staff actions are written to the audit log.
flags.confirmOn: Read-only mode blocks writes site-wide. Turn it on?
flags.mfaHint: When on, every staff member must set up and pass two-step verification before using the console. It can only be turned on once at least 2 staff members have set it up. Currently: {state}
flags.confirmMfaOn: Staff who haven't set up two-step verification will have to do so before using the console. Turn it on?
flags.confirmMfaOff: Staff without two-step verification will be able to use the console again (those who set it up still verify). Turn it off?

userAct.text: Target: {name}. Blocking, staff changes, unlinking and resetting two-step verification revoke current sessions; the user must sign in again.
userAct.recoverySent: Recovery email requested; ask the user to finish the reset on the forgot-password page

index.staffMfaLow: Fewer than 2 staff members have two-step verification set up. If someone loses their authenticator and recovery codes, nobody can reset it. Have another staff member finish setup.
index.mfaHint: Enable two-step verification: staff can block users and grant points, so a compromised account is costly.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.note: Dates use Taipei time and include the end date; action and entity type must match exactly.

mfa.title: Two-step verification
mfa.enabledPrompt: Enter the 6-digit code shown in your authenticator app.
mfa.intro: Once enabled, every console sign-in requires the 6-digit code from your authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, etc.).
mfa.lostPhone: If you lose your phone, sign in with a recovery code. If those are lost too, ask another staff member to reset it under Users in the console.
mfa.step1: 1. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, or enter the key manually:
mfa.step2: 2. Enter the 6-digit code shown in the app to finish enabling.
mfa.codesTitle: Two-step verification is on. Save these recovery codes:
mfa.codesHint: Each code works once and can stand in for a verification code if you lose your phone. They're shown only this once, so store them in a password manager or another safe place.
mfa.recoveryPrompt: Enter a recovery code you haven't used yet.
mfa.useRecovery: Don't have your phone? Use a recovery code
mfa.regenHint: All your old recovery codes will stop working.
mfa.skip: Skip for now, back to console

wallets.title: Point wallets
wallets.pointsLabel: Points (positive to grant, negative to deduct, within ±1,000,000 per action)
wallets.reasonLabel: Reason (required, recorded in ledger and audit log)
wallets.freezeNote: A frozen user can no longer contribute; existing contributions are unaffected.
wallets.insufficient: Balance would go negative (current balance {balance} pts)

orders.title: Order queue
orders.shippingTitle: Shipping info (reads are written to the audit log)
orders.amountLabel: Actual amount (required, must not exceed target {target})
orders.diffNote: Any amount below target is refunded to contributor wallets pro rata.
orders.failNote: All spent points are fully refunded to contributors; the item returns to funding (if not expired) or closed, and contributors are notified.
orders.deliveredNote: Confirm the parcel was delivered? The item will be marked fulfilled and contributors notified.
orders.refundedSuffix: ; difference of {points} pts refunded to contributors
orders.stale: Status was already updated; refresh and try again

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.privacy: Groups under 5 people show as <5 to prevent re-identification. Dates use Taipei time; staff and deleted accounts are excluded.
analytics.funnelNote: Cohort: users who signed up in the range; percentages are relative to the previous step.
analytics.retentionNote: Cohort: users who signed up in the range and whose observation window has ended.
analytics.retentionEmpty: No new users with a completed observation window in this range

cashRefunds.title: Cash refund review

confirm.completed: Confirm that the NT$ {amount} refund to {name} is done? This can't be undone.
confirm.rejected: Reject {name}'s {amount}-point request? The points go back to their original lots in the user's wallet.

cashRefunds.reasonLabel: Reject reason (required, shown to the user)
cashRefunds.rejectNote: A rejected request can't be restored; the user must submit a new one.

done.rejected: Rejected {name}'s request; {amount} points returned to their wallet

cashRefunds.stale: This request was changed by someone else. The list was reloaded.

walletDebts.title: Chargeback debts
walletDebts.intro: After a card chargeback, points that were already spent and can't be recovered are recorded as debt.

confirm.written_off: Write off {name}'s {amount}-point debt? The platform absorbs the loss and books it.

walletDebts.noteLabel: Note (required, saved to the audit log)
walletDebts.stale: This debt was already closed. The list was reloaded.

topups.title: Top-ups and chargeback disputes
topups.intro: On a card chargeback, marking a dispute freezes the wallet. Winning restores it; losing claws back what is left of that top-up lot and records the rest as debt.

confirm.open: Mark {name}'s NT$ {amount} top-up as disputed? The wallet will be frozen.
confirm.won: Dispute won for {name}'s NT$ {amount} top-up? It returns to paid, and the wallet is unfrozen if no other dispute is open.
confirm.lost: Chargeback lost for {name}'s NT$ {amount} top-up? The remaining points of that top-up lot are clawed back, the spent part is recorded as debt, and the wallet stays frozen.

done.open: Marked {name}'s NT$ {amount} top-up as disputed; wallet frozen
done.won: Marked {name}'s NT$ {amount} dispute as won; check the Wallets page for the wallet state
done.lost: Processed {name}'s NT$ {amount} chargeback: {recovered} points clawed back, {debt} points recorded as debt

topups.notApplied: This top-up had already changed state, so nothing was done ({name}, NT$ {amount}).
topups.stale: This top-up's state doesn't allow that action. The list was reloaded.

orgs.title: Org and permit review

confirm.approve: Approve "{name}"? It can then open relief sites.
confirm.needs_changes: Ask "{name}" for changes? The applicant will be notified.
confirm.reject: Reject "{name}"? The applicant can reapply after 30 days.
confirm.revoke2: Confirm again: revoking takes all public sites of "{name}" down immediately (back to draft). Revoke?
confirm.permitRevoke: Revoke approved permit {no}? Live sites using this permit will be paused.

orgs.stale: This record was updated by someone else; reloaded

events.title: Disaster events
events.mergeText: Merge "{name}" into another event? This cannot be undone.
events.hideText: Hide "{name}"? It will no longer show publicly.
events.targetNotFound: Event not found: enter an id, or a slug from the loaded list
events.selfMerge: Cannot merge an event into itself

finance.title: Finance
finance.soon: This tab is not available yet.

todo.title: To do
todo.note: Current state; not affected by the range. Click to handle.

kpi.title: Key figures
kpi.grossDef: Sum of top-ups whose payment notice arrived in the range, including ones later disputed or charged back; manual point grants excluded.
kpi.payersDef: Distinct wallets that topped up in the range.
kpi.firstTimeDef: Paying users whose first-ever payment falls in the range.

daily.title: Daily revenue
daily.note: By the date the payment notice arrived (Taipei time); may differ by a day from ECPay at day boundaries.
daily.aria: Line chart of daily top-up revenue
